headword: {完封勝利|かんぷうしょうり}

definitions.explanation: A victory in which the opposing team or player scores zero points or runs. Used primarily in baseball and other sports where preventing the opponent from scoring entirely is a notable achievement.

examples.japanese: エースが{完封勝利|かんぷうしょうり}を{収|おさ}めた。
examples.english: The ace pitcher achieved a shutout victory.

examples.japanese: {今季|こんき}{初|はつ}の{完封勝利|かんぷうしょうり}にチーム{全体|ぜんたい}が{喜|よろこ}んだ。
examples.english: The whole team celebrated their first shutout victory of the season.

examples.japanese: {若手|わかて}ピッチャーが{強豪|きょうごう}チームを{相手|あいて}に{見事|みごと}な{完封勝利|かんぷうしょうり}を{果|は}たし、{一躍|いちやく}スターになった。
examples.english: The young pitcher achieved a brilliant shutout victory against a powerhouse team and became a star overnight.

notes:
Composed of {完封|かんぷう} (shutout; holding scoreless) and {勝利|しょうり} (victory). Most commonly used in baseball, where a pitcher who completes a full game without allowing any runs earns a {完封勝利|かんぷうしょうり}. Also used in soccer and other team sports.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {完封勝利|かんぷうしょうり}を{収|おさ}める: to achieve a shutout victory
- {完封勝利|かんぷうしょうり}を{果|は}たす: to accomplish a shutout victory
- {完封勝利|かんぷうしょうり}を{飾|かざ}る: to cap off with a shutout victory

RELATED WORDS:
- {完封|かんぷう}: shutout — the act of holding the opponent scoreless
- {完封負|かんぷうま}け: shutout loss — being held scoreless
- {完投|かんとう}: complete game — pitching the entire game (may or may not be a shutout)
- {圧勝|あっしょう}: overwhelming victory — winning by a large margin, but not necessarily a shutout
